aspectTitle: Non-excepted content forces a horizontal scrollbar at 320 CSS px (fixed-width container, non-wrapping layout, layout-table-as-prose)
aspectDescription: The defining 1.4.10 failure: when the page is rendered at a width equivalent to 320 CSS px (the 1280px-at-400% equivalent), some section of NON-excepted content forces two-dimensional scrolling. Triggers include a fixed-width container (e.g. width:680px), a body/wrapper min-width, a flex/grid row that refuses to wrap, absolutely-positioned off-canvas content, or a layout table (a <table> used only to position prose side-by-side) that wrongly relies on the data-table exception. The viewport meta is permissive so b4f0c3 passes, yet the rendered page fails Reflow. The judgment that survives autom
scenario: Independent food-writing essay (Cadence Kitchen Journal) whose article body is hard-pinned to width:680px (not max-width); masthead and footer are fluid. At a 320 CSS-px viewport the whole page gains a horizontal scrollbar and every line of plain prose runs off the right edge.
mechanism: Fixed-width container: .article{width:680px} cannot shrink below 680px, so document scrollWidth (680) exceeds the 320px viewport. Non-excepted running prose (no table/map/media) requires two-dimensional scrolling to read line by line — verified at 320px: scrollWidth=680, prose paragraphs and h2 overflow.

aspectTitle: F102 — content/functionality present at desktop width disappears at 320px and is not reachable by any equivalent mechanism
aspectDescription: The dedicated failure technique F102: a section visible at 1280px is hidden at 320px (via display:none in a max-width media query, a collapsed sidebar, a responsive nav that drops links, a search field that vanishes, labels replaced by placeholders) WITHOUT providing the same or equivalent content through a disclosure widget, hamburger menu, dialog, icon, or link to another view. The page reflows (no horizontal scroll) and the viewport meta is fine, so it looks compliant to a tool, but information or functionality has been lost. Judging it requires comparing the desktop and narrow renderings,
scenario: Long-form coastal-news investigation: a sticky right-hand 'Continue this investigation' rail holds eight hand-curated related-story links that exist nowhere else. At max-width:600px the page reflows to a clean single column but the rail is display:none, and the eight links are reproduced nowhere — no disclosure, no section index, no inline list. On a phone or at 400% zoom the follow-up investigation is unreachable.
mechanism: Eight unique navigational <a> links (the only place they appear) are removed from the rendering and the accessibility tree by a media-query display:none at 320px, with no repositioned copy, disclosure, dialog, or link to another view — content available at desktop width is unavailable after reflow (F102).

aspectTitle: Long unbroken strings (URLs, tokens, hashes, paths, emails, compound words) overflow at 320px without wrapping or a reveal alternative
aspectDescription: Technique C33 addresses long sets of characters with no spaces — a displayed full URL, an API/auth key, a long hash, a deep file path, a blockchain address, a German compound word — that the browser cannot wrap (no break opportunities and no overflow-wrap:break-word / word-break applied, or white-space:nowrap forced). At 320px the one string punches out a horizontal scrollbar even though every paragraph around it reflows perfectly. The viewport meta is fine and the page is 99% fluid, so a viewport-string check sees nothing. The judgment: render at 320px to find the single overflowing element,
scenario: Help-center password-reset article displays a complete 180-char reset URL (domain + params + opaque JWT-style token) as the visible text of an inline link, in a fully fluid single-column layout. Rendered at 320px the link is 1168px wide and forces a page-level horizontal scrollbar while every paragraph reflows. Head case (head distribution).
mechanism: A long no-space token segment inside a URL has no break opportunity and the link has NO overflow-wrap/word-break, so at a 320 CSS px viewport the single <a> overflows horizontally; probe confirmed document width 1204px and that neutralizing only a.verify-link returns the page to exactly 320px (sole offender). Low-vision/400%-zoom users must scroll in two dimensions to read the link, the barrier C33 addresses.

aspectTitle: Two-dimensional-layout exception over-claimed or mis-scoped: non-excepted surroundings of a table/map/grid fail to reflow
aspectDescription: 1.4.10 exempts sections that genuinely require two-dimensional layout (data tables, maps, diagrams, grids, code where indentation is meaningful, presentations). The judgment-heavy failure mode is mis-scoping: a developer lets the WHOLE page scroll in two dimensions 'because there's a table', so the heading, intro paragraph, search field, and pagination that surround the table — none of which need 2D layout — also extend off-screen and require horizontal scrolling. The Understanding doc shows exactly this pass/fail pair. Conversely, flagging content that legitimately IS a data table/map/video w
scenario: Municipal treasury property-levy register: a genuine 9-column data table is legitimately excepted, but body{min-width:980px} drags the H1, intro paragraph, search field, and pagination off-screen at 320px. aspectTitle: Sticky / fixed-position content (headers, footers, cookie bars, chat widgets, ads) consumes or obscures the 320x256 viewport so reflowed content cannot be read
aspectDescription: Headers, footers, toolbars, cookie banners, chat widgets, and fixed ads that are reasonable at desktop become viewport-eating obstructions when zoomed to a 320px-wide / 256px-tall viewport. A sticky 130px-tall header over a 256px-tall viewport leaves almost nothing to read; a fixed-bottom cookie bar plus fixed-top nav can sandwich content into a sliver; a fixed-corner ad can cover the focused link, providing no way to dismiss it without keyboard-navigating to its close button. The Understanding doc's Focus-Not-Obscured overlap section and technique C34 both call for un-fixing these at small si
scenario: A coastal newspaper long-form article with a position:sticky masthead (wordmark + section nav + dateline, min-height:130px). The article reflows to a single 320px-wide column with zero horizontal overflow, but at the 256px reflow HEIGHT the sticky masthead renders 212px tall, consuming 83% of the viewport and leaving a ~44px sliver to read in.
mechanism: A persistent position:sticky region sized for desktop occupies 83% of the 256px reflow viewport height, so a low-vision user who zooms can read only 2-3 lines at a time and must scroll a near-full screen per couple of lines — the loss-of-function the SC prevents. C34 (un-fix at small height) is not applied.

aspectTitle: Horizontally-scrolling carousel where an individual panel does not fit within 320 CSS px (G225)

The Understanding doc gives a pass (each home-listing panel fits 320px) and a fail (the second panel's content does not fit 320px). The failure is subtle: the carousel mechanism is fine and most panels fit, but one over-stuffed panel (longer text, an extra-wide image, a wider card) forces horizontal scrolling WITHIN that panel. Catching it requires rendering at 32
scenario: E-commerce outdoor-gear product carousel (flex overflow-x:auto strip). Four product cards are width:300px and read top-to-bottom; one featured 'Trail Pack Bundle' promo card is hard-coded width:420px with a 396px inner image and a no-wrap price/save row, so that single panel cannot fit a 320px viewport and forces within-panel horizontal scrolling.

Rendered at 320px: the .card.promo panel is 420px wide (widerThanViewport=true) while all four sibling .card panels are 300px and fit.
